_meta.purpose: The editorial brief for every content page — the editor's standard orchestration of key info: Explainer (what this is), Research (how made + honesty note), References (sources), Documentation (method). page-brief.js auto-loads the entry for the current filename. Utility/app pages (index map, hero, 3D canvases, privacy, sitemap) are intentionally omitted. Sourced-or-gap: a page with no entry simply shows no brief.

ancient-india.html.explainer: Five thousand years of India on one spine — each era read on five facets (language, script, people, rulers, heritage), with the evidence behind every fact open to interrogation.
ancient-india.html.research: Built from peer-reviewed ancient-DNA papers (Narasimhan & Shinde 2019), Ashoka's own edicts, and paleography. Each fact carries an evidence tier and a 'shaped by the winner' check; contested points (e.g. the Aryan-migration narrative) are flagged, not resolved.

ashoka.html.explainer: The reach and the ethics of Mauryan rule, read from Ashoka's own edicts — a ruler you can verify because the script was deciphered.
ashoka.html.research: Edict find-spots mapped from the archaeological record; texts summarised from standard translations (Hultzsch 1925). Edicts are treated as the ruler's own words AND propaganda — kept apart from later Buddhist legend.

scripts.html.explainer: Two family trees kept apart: how India's languages descend (Indo-Aryan vs Dravidian) and how their scripts descend (nearly all from Brahmi) — with the modern Bharati link-script.
scripts.html.research: Compiled from paleography and historical linguistics; Brahmi's contested parentage is flagged, not resolved. Every script renders in a self-hosted OFL font so specimens never break.

vedas.html.explainer: One source text opened across languages — the Rigveda's Hymn of Creation in Sanskrit, romanised, glossed word-by-word, and compared across attributed translations.
vedas.html.research: Sanskrit from Wikisource; translations are real, published and credited (Griffith 1896, Basham 1954). Languages without a sourced translation are shown as honest gaps — never machine-invented.

languages.html.explainer: The hub for every language and script of Bharat — families, scripts, self-hosted fonts, and source texts, all in one place.
languages.html.research: Language-family assignments from standard linguistics; each language shown in its own script via bundled OFL Noto fonts. Real, attributed translations only; gaps marked, never machine-filled.

journey.html.explainer: A scroll-through journey following one word across 4,000 years — from unwritten proto-languages, through Brahmi, to the living languages of today.
journey.html.research: A narrative built on the same sourced family-tree and script data as the languages pages; reconstructed proto-forms are labelled as reconstructions, not attested words.

deep-history.html.explainer: What ancient DNA reveals about who migrated, mixed and was replaced across the subcontinent — from Neanderthals to the Steppe and the Indus genome.
deep-history.html.research: Held strictly to peer-reviewed ancient-DNA science (Reich lab; Narasimhan & Shinde 2019). A genetic finding (established) is kept separate from a historical interpretation (the 'Aryan migration' debate is flagged contested).

heritage-atlas.html.explainer: Sacred ground across Bharat — temples and sites with their builders, lifespans and record of destruction; Sanatan, Jain, Buddhist and contested.
heritage-atlas.html.research: Sites compiled from public heritage records; builder and destruction claims are multi-actor and attributed, not one-sided. 'Sanatan Dharma' preferred over 'Hindu' per the project's usage.

atrocities.html.explainer: History's 100 deadliest events, rebuilt as an interactive timeline and world map — with India's events highlighted.
atrocities.html.research: Figures from Matthew White's 'Great Big Book of Horrible Things' (the NYT 'Population Control, Marauder Style' chart). Tolls for ancient events are wide estimates and shown as such.

feed.html.explainer: The record behind the headlines — news clustered by place, with a media-lean bar next to the spin-proof numbers.
feed.html.research: Coverage aggregated and attributed; media-lean is contested and labelled as such. Facts (population, per-capita, crime, prisons) are sourced-or-gap, shown beside the framing.

timeline.html.explainer: Events over time — the fiscal and civic record, on a scrubbable timeline.
timeline.html.research: Events drawn from the district ledger and fiscal-events data; each entry links to its source or is marked a gap.

state-of-india.html.explainer: Who carries the country — every state ranked on the active fiscal view.
state-of-india.html.research: State figures from the district ledger, aggregated; the ranking changes with the chosen dimension. Sourced-or-gap throughout.

explore.html.explainer: Filter and rank all 594 districts on any dimension — a client-side query engine over the whole ledger.
explore.html.research: Runs entirely in the browser over the sourced district ledger; a district with no figure for a dimension is shown as a gap, not a zero.

command-chain.html.explainer: Who answers to whom — the federal / state / union chain of command that moves public money.
command-chain.html.research: The 4-layer decode is built from the constitutional/administrative structure; it maps the protocol, not individual officials' conduct.

encroachment-atlas.html.explainer: Built where water returns — illegal habitation on flood-prone and reclaimed land, case by case.
encroachment-atlas.html.research: Encroachment cases and flood exposure from public records and open terrain/flood-plain data; each case is attributed.

quake-tsunami.html.explainer: A live earthquake and tsunami tracker — real-time USGS feed alongside historical quakes and tsunamis.
quake-tsunami.html.research: Live data from the USGS earthquake feed; historical events from compiled catalogues. Live values are as-reported and may revise.

terrain-3d.html.explainer: District terrain in 2D and 3D — relief, rivers and flood plain over real elevation.
terrain-3d.html.research: Built from open elevation (DEM) and river/flood data; an honest upscale, not sharper-than-source imagery.

flood-3d.html.explainer: A flood explorer — watch water rise over real district terrain.
flood-3d.html.research: Water levels modelled over open DEM terrain; a visualisation of exposure, not a hydrological prediction.

global.html.explainer: India against the world — GDP, income and industry compared across countries.
global.html.research: Indicators from the World Bank open data; India is the reference, other countries the comparison.

geopolitical-chess.html.explainer: The dollar is the board — a framing of world players, who rules each, what they bring, and how it's entangled.
geopolitical-chess.html.research: Sourced facts (ruling party, power nexus, pieces) are labelled; the 'chess' framing is explicitly OUR framing, not a claim of fact. Client/puppet-state calls are flagged as interpretation.

engines.html.explainer: The seven composable lenses — Survey, Country, Development, Climate, Zoning, Corruption, News — the method behind the atlas.
engines.html.research: A framework page: each engine is a way of reading the same sourced data, not a new dataset.

heritage-3d.html.explainer: Temples and ruins as 3D photogrammetry models you can turn in the browser.
heritage-3d.html.research: Models are third-party photogrammetry (Sketchfab), embedded and attributed to their authors.

cave-walk.html.explainer: Walk inside a reconstructed temple in the first person — Ajanta, Ellora and Nagara forms, as they once were.
cave-walk.html.research: Reconstructions are interpretive rebuilds of temple forms, not scans of the ruins as they stand today; built to documented architectural types.

temple-forms.html.explainer: Temple architecture types and orientation, modelled to real sourced dimensions.
temple-forms.html.research: Each archetype is built by a reproducible script to sourced dimensions (temple_dims.json); a math-accurate model, not a specific building.

history.html.explainer: A history race — states rising and falling on the chosen measure, over time.
history.html.research: Animated from the same sourced state figures used across the atlas; a presentation of the data, not new data.

library.html.explainer: A reading room — public-domain memoirs and primary sources of the Nehru age, with a scrollytelling journey.
library.html.research: Texts are public-domain works served via Archive.org; presented, not edited.

provenance.html.explainer: The provenance ledger — every figure traced to its citation, audited for zero unattributed numbers.
provenance.html.research: Generated by walking the ledger and safety data against their sources; this page IS the audit trail.

knowledge.html.explainer: The knowledge base — a catalogue of every dataset the atlas holds.
knowledge.html.research: Auto-generated from the data catalogue so it can't drift from what's actually shipped.

mesh.html.explainer: The mesh — how the atlas's places, money and events connect, as a network.
mesh.html.research: A graph view over the existing sourced relationships; a lens, not new data.

globe-map.html.explainer: Watch the globe unroll into a flat map — a live projection morph.
globe-map.html.research: A real projection transform over open outline data; a demonstration of how map projections distort.

geopolitics.html.research: Sourced facts labelled; framing labelled as framing.
